requirements.requirement: Operate DNSSEC-signed infra.test with node1 as primary and node2/node3 as authoritative secondaries.
requirements.summary: Node1 reports a dynamic, secure, automatically maintained inline-signed primary. Both configured secondaries return authoritative DNSKEY, RRSIG, and zone data, and all three finish active with the same signed serial.

requirements.requirement: Publish app.infra.test as node1's service address and status.infra.test as TXT "ready".
requirements.summary: Node1's observed address is 10.100.160.10, and the final primary, both secondaries, and node4 return app.infra.test A 10.100.160.10 and status.infra.test TXT "ready".

requirements.requirement: Accept authenticated updates from node1 and propagate changes to both secondaries.
requirements.summary: An unauthenticated update was refused and remained absent. TSIG-authenticated updates were accepted, signed, and observed on both secondaries, including a second update after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Configure node4 to resolve infra.test through both secondaries.
requirements.summary: Node4's final forwarding configuration and persistent resolver settings contain both secondary addresses. It returns DNSSEC-validated answers, and traffic was directly observed reaching node3 while node2 was unavailable.

requirements.requirement: Keep resolution available when one authoritative server is unavailable.
requirements.summary: Both secondaries and node4 were healthy at baseline; node2 was then stopped with its DNS listener absent. After a cache flush, node4 still returned validated app and status answers, node3 logged serving them, and node2 was restored with current data.

overall_summary: All five material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. DNSSEC authority, requested records, authenticated replication, node4 resolution, and bounded single-server failover all worked. The separate provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on all four nodes and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Node4's use of node3 was directly path-traced during the outage, but there is no equivalent node4-to-node2 query log; node2's upstream role is supported by node4's configuration and node2's direct authoritative health.
The bounded availability exercise stopped node2 only; separate node1 and node3 outage permutations were not captured.
No final firewall-rule listing was captured, although cross-node DNS behavior and post-reboot listeners demonstrate the required service paths.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had a clear installation, configuration, bounded verification, mandatory-restart, or restoration role; no unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Query logging was turned back off, and the node2 disruption was fully restored. Minor avoidable residue remained: the update-check and persistence-check TXT records were created for valid update/replication evidence but were not deleted afterward. All four restart protocols contain a healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state; fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate them. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services and healthy package-manager state on every node.
